channel.title: Audio-Generation on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Audio-Generation on Best of AI

item.title: Eleven v4
item.description: ElevenLabs launched Eleven v4 on September 28, 2026, improving expressiveness and voice cloning (down to a 10-second sample) across more than 90 languages. Eleven v4 Turbo is the same model tuned for real-time use, running at roughly 100 milliseconds of median latency. Eleven v4 ranked first on the Artificial Analysis Provider Voice Arena leaderboard for September 2026, with about 75% of listeners preferring it over five rival services in blind tests.

item.title: Nemotron 3 Diarization
item.description: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3 Diarization on September 23, 2026, a 100-million-parameter open-weight model that tracks up to eight overlapping speakers in real-time streaming audio. It targets call-center and meeting-transcription pipelines that need to know who said what as the audio comes in, rather than after the fact.

item.title: Qwen-Audio-3.1-Realtime
item.description: Alibaba released Qwen-Audio-3.1-Realtime on September 28, 2026 as the flagship of a five-model Qwen-Audio-3.1 stack that also covers speech recognition and text-to-speech. It’s built for full-duplex voice agents, meaning it can listen and respond at the same time and decide mid-conversation when to speak versus when to call an external tool.

item.title: Eleven Multilingual v2
item.description: Eleven Multilingual v2 is the speech synthesis model ElevenLabs shipped when it moved its text-to-speech product out of beta, in August 2023. It generates natural-sounding speech across 29 languages, including Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hindi, and most major European languages, while preserving a cloned voice’s character between languages. Compared to ElevenLabs’ faster Flash and Turbo models, Multilingual v2 trades speed for quality: it’s meant for narration, dubbing, audiobooks, and other content where the audio gets published rather than streamed live in a conversation. It remains one of ElevenLabs’ most widely used models for voice cloning and dubbing workflows even after the company released Eleven v3.
